source.title: Autoformalization with Large Language Models
source.authors: Yu-Huai Wu; Albert Qiaochu Jiang; Wen-Da Li; M. Rabe; Charles Staats; M. Jamnik; C. Szegedy

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether model scale improves performance on an evaluated task, using autoformalization BLEU scores and correctness judgments rather than held-out language-model loss.
record.gate_note: The paper reports autoformalization results across PaLM model sizes, which bear on downstream predictability. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy, fit power laws, test extrapolation of loss, or evaluate compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. The cited language-model scaling results are not study results.
record.test_reason: A side result in a new setting. Table 1 reports autoformalization BLEU for PaLM 8B, 64B and 540B, and Case Study 2 compares the three sizes on one problem. Both bear on V6: downstream performance improving with scale. The study fits no curve, measures no loss, and runs no training sweeps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only the scaling side result. The main conclusions are different. LLMs (Codex) perfectly formalize 25.3% of 150 sampled competition problems into Isabelle/HOL. Training a neural prover on autoformalized statements raises the miniF2F test proof rate from 29.6% to 35.2%. Scaling PaLM improving BLEU is a secondary observation.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates formalization quality and correctness across pretrained model sizes; it does not measure held-out language-model loss, fit a power law, or perform compute-optimal training sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The study notes that few-shot examples matter: a tangentially related prompt example enables Codex to formalize the linear-function problem correctly. It does not quantify that prompt change in the BLEU table.

fits_no_version.finding: Codex scores above every tested PaLM size on BLEU in both subjects (57.13 and 43.33).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data composition (more formal or code data) can outweigh model size on formal-language translation tasks.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is limited to two autoformalization subjects and BLEU scores, with no uncertainty estimates or fitted predictive relationship. A separate size comparison is a single case-study problem.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss is measured.
No fitted law and no extrapolation.
No other modality or training regime is analysed for power-law form.
Untested: performance against pretraining loss, a fitted or extrapolated scaling curve, uncertainty, and any size beyond three PaLM checkpoints.

record.verdict_notes: The tranche changes from T2 to T3: this is a new downstream setting, not a different method on the original question. The scale evidence is three PaLM checkpoints with no uncertainty estimates. Gains per 8x size step shrink (+11.6 and +7.2 BLEU on algebra), but the study does not analyse this.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs’ held-out loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their trends with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests scale-related performance on autoformalization, but does not test downstream performance against pretraining loss or establish a predictive scaling curve.
Dependence of fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup or fitting choices.

relationships.condition: PaLM 8B/64B/540B, few-shot autoformalization BLEU on miniF2F algebra and number_theory
relationships.reason: BLEU rises monotonically with size in both subjects: 31.49→43.13→50.30 and 22.10→31.43→36.16 (r1–r6). This is only three points, with no predictive fit.
relationships.display_finding: BLEU increased monotonically through 31.49→43.13→50.30 for algebra and 22.10→31.43→36.16 for number theory, although only three sizes were evaluated without a predictive fit.

relationships.condition: Single Case Study 2 problem, greedy decoding, PaLM 8B/64B/540B
relationships.reason: Only 540B formalizes the problem correctly; 8B and 64B fail (r9–r11). This is one anecdotal example, consistent with improvement at scale.
relationships.display_finding: Only the 540B model formalized the problem correctly; the 8B and 64B models failed on this single example.
